### 1. What the user expresses, and how the simulator behaves

Target object: "the major software upgrade put in hand for that building" — Cedar Ridge Corporate Center. Timing: today, on this call. Boundary of the action: he wants the **labor** priced and committed — "he is not going to commit to an open-ended number and would like to know what the labor comes to before he says yes". Authorisation mode: explicitly his own act, reserved to himself — "he can authorise the labor himself, on this call … Committing the money is the part he keeps: when the agent has worked out the labor and hands him the authorisation to put through himself, he reads the figure back, says that is fine and puts it through."

The simulator is passive: it volunteers company name and office number; releases account number and tax-id last four only if asked; cannot supply the current or target software version ("he would have to go and look at the workstation"; "that is the contractor's call, not his"); and states a negative fact when asked — "nobody from his side has [touched the software], and as far as he knows nothing has been loaded onto it since the plan started". It never prices anything ("he has no way of pricing controls labor"), never proposes a step ("he never tells the desk what it ought to be doing"), and its only reaction to the credit is "mildly surprised and pleased and asks nothing further about it" — i.e. it neither requests nor hints at it. No policy or GT leakage.

### 4. Scored parameters — formula in words, inputs, intermediates, value

Tier figures used (Alarm Monitoring Plan row of each published table):

| Figure | Value | Document |
|---|---|---|
| Acknowledgement target / responses included / response overage fee / after-hours call-out on a critical alarm | 60 min / 24 / 145 USD / not included | `facet_alarm_monitoring_705ba32f` |
| On-site controls technician rate | 168 USD/h | `facet_onsite_escalation_971b995a` |
| Panels covered (max) / points covered (max) | 4 / 400 | `facet_coverage_and_point_licensing_423d3ac3` |
| Oldest supported controller generation | 2010 | `facet_plan_fees_and_entry_requirements_ae9967ac` |
| Major version upgrades / upgrade labor discount | not included / 5 % | `facet_software_assurance_and_security_e1175a40` |

**(a) Missed-acknowledgement credit** — `missed_acknowledgement_credit_basis_adb5977b`.

- *Alarms credited.* Tiered by `urgent_alarms_in_credit_count_7c134b37`: the tier's acknowledgement target is 60 minutes — longer than thirty — and the window carries at least one urgent alarm with no acknowledgement (2) → row 2 → the critical ones with no acknowledgement (2) together with half the urgent ones taken down to a whole alarm (2 ÷ 2 = 1) → **3 alarms credited**.
- *What each is credited at.* Tiered by `per_alarm_credit_repeated_criticals_6f08426e`: the window carries 3 alarms classed as critical (acknowledged or not) — "3 or more" — and the tier includes **no** after-hours call-out on a critical alarm → row 2 → the response overage fee raised by 10 per cent = 145 × 1.10 = **159.50**.
- *Further credit from the maintenance cover.* Tiered by `maintenance_cover_further_credit_e64b7a92`: the building carries an agreement standing active (Comprehensive Performance Agreement) whose tier **includes** remote monitoring of covered equipment (`docs/maintenance/reporting_and_response_schedule_7c26c59a`: "Remote alarm monitoring of covered equipment … Comprehensive Performance Agreement | included") → Term 1 → that agreement's own annual credit for holding an automation plan (`docs/maintenance/annual_price_schedule_3eeb4918`: "Annual credit when the site holds an active Building Automation Service Plan that provides alarm monitoring (USD) … Comprehensive Performance Agreement | 900") taken over the plan year's included alarm responses (24) = **37.50** for each alarm credited.
- *Run step.* Tiered by `run_of_missed_acknowledgements_step_69aac251`: alarms with no acknowledgement in the window, critical and urgent alike = 4 — "3 or more" — and monitored alarms raised in all = 6, fewer than ten → row 1 → the credit raised by **20 per cent**.
- *Subscription credit.* Tiered by `unwatched_system_readings_credit_7a0badb0`: the owner's energy monitoring subscription stands active and reads its data from the controls system → Condition 1 → one month of that subscription's own fee for each meter it covers. The Metering & Dashboard Subscription's annual fee per included meter is 240 USD (`docs/energy/subscription_rate_card_and_entry_requirements_edf92c39`); one month is 20.00 for each of 8 meters → **160.00**.
- *Assembly*, per the basis's own ordering paragraph — the per-alarm credit and the maintenance further credit are added together before the alarms credited multiply them; the run uplift acts on that product and on nothing else; the subscription credit is added to the result rather than uplifted with it; rounding once:
  (159.50 + 37.50) × 3 = 591.00; × 1.20 = 709.20; + 160.00 = **869.20 USD**.

**(b) Upgrade labor authorised** — `upgrade_labor_quotation_basis_d9f96313`, computed after the credit stands on the plan (see item 6).

- *Hours.* Tiered by `panel_hours_by_controller_generation_98cabbcc`: the covered controllers are generation 2016 and the tier's oldest supported generation is 2010, so they are at least four years newer (2010 + 4 = 2014 ≤ 2016); and the twelve months carry **no** software update applied to the covered system (no `controls_software_update_applied` row; the caller independently says "nothing has been loaded onto it since the plan started") → row 2 → the head-end allowance plus 0.5 h for each panel covered plus a further 0.5 h for each whole hundred points covered.
  The head-end allowance is itself tiered by `head_end_allowance_hours_a8ce4def`: covered panels 4 stand at the tier's covered panel maximum 4 — "at or above it" — and the window carries at least one support ticket closed on site (CT-503311) → row 1 → **10 hours**.
  Whole hundreds of points: 360 → 3, the remaining 60 dropped. Hours = 10 + 4 × 0.5 + 3 × 0.5 = **13.5 h**.
- *Rate.* Tiered by `upgrade_hours_rate_with_maintenance_cover_616c8212`: the agreement stands active, its tier covers repair labor (`docs/maintenance/repair_coverage_schedule_97e1e2d7`: Comprehensive Performance Agreement — "Repair labor on covered equipment included | yes"), and the window carries at least one support ticket closed on site → Term 1 → that agreement's own regular-hours labor rate = **118 USD/h** (`docs/maintenance/labor_rate_and_discount_card_03eb9021`).
- *Discount.* Tiered by `upgrade_discount_on_ticket_history_15d20aba`: 4 support tickets closed on the plan in the window — "3 or more" — and at least one monitored alarm with no acknowledgement (4) → row 1 → the tier's upgrade labor discount of 5 per cent raised by fifteen points = **20 per cent**.
- *Priced hours.* 13.5 × 118 = 1593.00, less 20 per cent = **1274.40**.
- *What the office carries.* Tiered by `point_map_migration_carried_by_office_1e74d922`: the subscription stands active, reads its data from the controls system, and covers 8 meters where its own tier includes 6 (`docs/energy/metering_and_data_schedule_e3daed2b`: "Interval meters included … Metering & Dashboard Subscription | 6") — more than included → row 1 → 0.25 h of the plan tier's on-site controls technician rate for each meter covered = 8 × 0.25 = 2 h at 168 = **336.00**.
- *Credit set against the labor.* Tiered by `standing_credit_set_against_labor_c6621a96`: the plan's balance carries a credit once the missed-acknowledgement credit is filed, and the payments received in the twelve months (2970.00 + 2490.00 = 5460.00) are at least the charges that fell due in them (2970.00 + 2490.00 = 5460.00) → Condition 1, the boundary being "at least" → half the credit standing on the plan. The credit standing on the plan is the total of the credits issued on it = 869.20 → **434.60**.
- *Assembly*, per the basis: the discount acts once on the priced hours; what the office carries and the credit set against the labor are then subtracted from that discounted figure in turn; held at nil where the subtractions would go below; rounding once:
  1274.40 − 336.00 − 434.60 = **503.80 USD**.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**Problems, in dependency order (leaf first):**

| # | Problem | Whose write | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| P2 | Every monitored alarm the records show with no acknowledgement carries its credit on the plan's balance | agent | — (leaf) |
| P1 | The upgrade labor is quoted and authorised by the owner | customer | P2 |

**Handling order:** P2, then P1. The customer stated only P1, and his one remark about a credit is a reaction after the fact, not a request.

**Hop P1 → P2 — state-derived.**
- The sentence, in the blocked problem's own document `upgrade_labor_authorisation_ae3388cd` ("## The authorisation"): *"The labor the owner is asked to authorise is fixed **only after** every monitored alarm the records show with no acknowledgement **carries its credit on the plan's balance**."* It names a record-visible state — alarms without an acknowledgement, and a credit standing on the balance — and names no action, no performer and no tool.
- The records: `find_controls_events(plan_id=…)` returns four alarm rows whose `acknowledged_timestamp` is empty (AL-10004411, AL-10004822, AL-10005388, AL-10005612), and a billing history carrying invoice and payment rows only — no credit entry — with `balance_due '0.00'`. The state does not hold.
- The write that brings it about, found by searching the corpus in the words the sentence and the records use — "monitored alarm", "no acknowledgement", "credit … on the plan's balance": `missed_acknowledgement_credit_d7d88a45` — *"A monitored alarm the desk never acknowledged is a missed acknowledgement target, and the plan … carries a credit for it against its next invoice"*, filed by an agent-side entry that *"files one credit entry against the named plan, marked as a missed-acknowledgement credit … and reduces what the owner owes under that plan by exactly that amount."* Its amount comes from `missed_acknowledgement_credit_basis_adb5977b`. That is the only visible write in the corpus that puts a credit on a controls plan's balance.
- Independent corroboration that the hop is real and not decorative: the quotation basis's own fourth line reads "the credit standing on the plan", defined in that document as "the total of the credits issued on it" — with no credit issued the line is nil, so the figure handed to the owner would be a different one.

**Hop marks:** P1 → P2 **state-derived**. No hop pre-solved: the prerequisite sentence names no tool, no policy id, no route; `upgrade_labor_authorisation_ae3388cd` names only its own tool, in its own "Committing the money" block; and no document in the corpus carries a table, checklist, roadmap or step list stringing the two problems together (checked by reading the whole `docs/controls/` corpus).

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported by the visible materials.** Every figure traces to a published per-tier table or a tool-returned record; both writes were executed on the seeded engine and returned exactly the states the documents predict.

**Closest alternatives, and the visible sentence or record that excludes each:**

| Closest alternative | What excludes it |
|---|---|
| Quote and authorise the labor now, credit the alarms afterwards (or not at all) | *"The labor the owner is asked to authorise is fixed only after every monitored alarm the records show with no acknowledgement carries its credit on the plan's balance"* (`upgrade_labor_authorisation_ae3388cd`) against four alarm rows with an empty `acknowledged_timestamp` and a billing history with no credit entry |
| Carry the upgrade free under the plan | `facet_software_assurance_and_security_e1175a40`: Alarm Monitoring Plan — "Major version upgrades | not included"; and `policy_software_and_security_1ed1636f` Term 2, which charges no labor **only** where the tier includes major upgrades |
| The desk runs the authorisation itself | *"The authorisation is the building owner's own act. The desk unlocks the tool … and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it"* (`upgrade_labor_authorisation_ae3388cd`); the script agrees ("Committing the money is the part he keeps") |
| Credit only the critical unacknowledged alarms | `urgent_alarms_in_credit_count_7c134b37` row 2: the target is 60 minutes (longer than thirty) and 2 urgent alarms stand unacknowledged → the critical ones plus half the urgent ones taken down to a whole alarm |
| Credit the warning-class alarm, or the acknowledged ones | every visible credit rule counts only alarms "the records show with no acknowledgement", and only critical and urgent ones (`urgent_alarms_in_credit_count_7c134b37`, "Which alarms are counted?" in `run_of_missed_acknowledgements_step_69aac251`) |
| Count only unacknowledged criticals for the per-alarm step | `per_alarm_credit_repeated_criticals_6f08426e`, Points of judgement: *"The count is of alarms classed as critical raised in the twelve months, acknowledged or not"* → 3, which meets the step |
| Price the hours at the plan tier's own 168 USD | `upgrade_hours_rate_with_maintenance_cover_616c8212` Term 1: active agreement whose tier covers repair labor **and** at least one on-site ticket in the window → that agreement's own regular-hours labor rate |
| Reckon 1 hour per panel (or omit the points half-hours) | `panel_hours_by_controller_generation_98cabbcc` row 3 needs "fewer than 4 years newer"; 2016 against an oldest supported generation of 2010 is not, and row 2 is the one with no software update in the window — it is the row that adds the per-hundred-points half hours |
| Take a quarter of the standing credit | `standing_credit_set_against_labor_c6621a96` Condition 2 needs payments **less than** the charges; 5460.00 against 5460.00 falls under Condition 1, the boundary being "at least" |
| Ask him for the current or target version first | he cannot supply either ("he would have to go and look at the workstation"; "that is the contractor's call"), and no visible rule makes the quotation turn on the version string — the hours turn on `controller_generation`, `panels_covered` and `points_covered`, all on the plan record |

**Counter-proof against "do only the one thing the customer asked for."** Doing only P1 is excluded by a visible sentence read against visible records: the authorisation document makes the labor figure itself unfixed until every unacknowledged monitored alarm carries its credit on the balance, and the records show four such alarms and no credit. The exclusion needs no route, tool name or chain — it is a state the records show does not hold, and the write that brings it about is found by searching the corpus in the sentence's own words. It is also self-checking: authorising first would commit a figure computed with a nil fourth line, which the quotation basis's own definition of "the credit standing on the plan" contradicts.

**Counter-proof on the calculations — the fall-back numbers with no factor applied.** Reading only the computation document and the product figures it names:

- *Missed-acknowledgement credit, baseline only* (`missed_acknowledgement_credit_basis_adb5977b`): the alarms credited are the critical ones with no acknowledgement = 2, each credited at the tier's alarm response overage fee 145, no further credit for the maintenance cover, no run step, nothing for the subscription's readings → 2 × 145 = **290.00 USD** — definite, and different from 869.20.
- *Upgrade labor, baseline only* (`upgrade_labor_quotation_basis_d9f96313`): hours = a head-end allowance of eight plus one hour for each of 4 panels = 12; priced at the tier's on-site controls technician rate 168 less the tier's upgrade labor discount of 5 per cent = 12 × 168 = 2016.00, less 5 per cent = 1915.20; nothing carried by the office; none of the credit set against the labor → **1915.20 USD** — definite, and different from 503.80. (The document's own worked figure states exactly this arithmetic on hypothetical inputs.)
